items.label: Liquidity limit
items.title: The alarm is live. The vault is fully lent out.
items.body: An alarm can't create liquidity. Canopy withdraws whatever is liquid and keeps trying while the alarm is live, but there may be nothing to withdraw.

items.label: False alarms
items.title: A warning turns out to be wrong.
items.body: An unneeded exit gives up your position. Requiring two signals reduces false fires, but can't remove them.

items.label: No swap at launch
items.title: The stablecoin itself is the problem.
items.body: You get the vault's own asset. An exit from a vault in a failing stablecoin doesn't help, so Canopy doesn't offer that alarm on those vaults.

items.label: Permission model
items.title: A keeper runs the exit.
items.body: The keeper can't choose a payout address. The contract pays the position owner. Contract risk still applies.

items.label: Protocol restrictions
items.title: The vault turns on a share gate.
items.body: A curator can switch on share-transfer gates that block the standard exit. The app reads each vault's gates and won't arm one that would block you.

items.label: Separate billing
items.title: A plan payment lapses.
items.body: The exit contract has no fee logic. Canopy's keepers run paid wallets, and anyone can run an exit for an armed position with the open-source keeper. Exit Now stays free.

items.label: AI boundary
items.title: A report gets an AI label.
items.body: The AI only labels public reports. It can't fire an alarm, choose an amount or pick where funds go.

items.label: Crowded exits
items.title: Many people armed the same vault.
items.body: Exits race each other for the same liquidity. Being first stops being an edge when everyone is armed.

items.label: Your controls
items.title: You decide to stop using Canopy.
items.body: One transaction disarms every position. You can also revoke the vault approval and withdraw directly, as usual.

items.question: What does Canopy do, and what is live now?
items.answer: Canopy watches the DeFi vaults you hold and tries to exit them to your own wallet when an alarm you chose fires. Auto-exit is live on Robinhood Chain for ERC-4626 vaults. Checking a wallet is free and needs no connection.

items.question: Can AI or a keeper choose where my funds go?
items.answer: No. The exit contract has no "send to" field and pays the position owner only. The AI only labels public reports; your alarm rules and the contracts decide what happens. Contract risk still applies.

items.question: Will every exit succeed?
items.answer: No. A fully lent-out vault, a share gate, a pause or a bug can limit or stop a withdrawal, and false alarms can cause unneeded exits. Canopy withdraws what is liquid and keeps trying while the alarm is live. It promises no outcome and does not pay for losses.

items.question: What do I pay, and can I revoke access?
items.answer: Scanning, risk cards and alerts are free. The Armed plan is $15 for 3 months or $60 a year per wallet, paid in USDG, and keepers pay the gas. Exit Now and Disarm All are always free. One transaction disarms everything, and you can revoke the vault approval.

items.question: I hold this vault through Robinhood Earn. Can I use Canopy?
items.answer: You can check your position and follow the vault for free alerts. Auto-exit needs a wallet you sign with yourself, so it doesn't work for positions held in the Robinhood app. Alerts tell you to withdraw there.

items.question: Do I need an account or my seed phrase?
items.answer: No. Canopy never asks for a seed phrase, a login or any ID. Your browser builds every transaction, and you sign it in your own wallet.
